title: Storage consumer prematurely cancels after 30s causing buffer saturation and runaway downloading
description:
## Problem Statement

When running the application in download mode (`dotnet run --project .\src\Eetaa.Worker\ --mode=download`), the `SingleWriterStorageEngine` consumer stops processing after exactly 30 seconds due to a cancellation request. However, `SettlementIngestionService` continues downloading files indefinitely while no records are being persisted.

The channel buffer saturates at capacity (1000 items), items/s rate degrades towards 0, and the application hangs in an unrecoverable state until manually terminated via SIGINT/Ctrl+C.

## Observed Console Capture

```text
┌ georg@phoebe  eetaa   develop ≢ ?1 
└ $ dotnet run --project .\src\Eetaa.Worker\ --mode=download
Using launch settings from .\src\Eetaa.Worker\Properties\launchSettings.json...
Building...
[09:15:59 INF] Worker starting in mode: download, db: data/eetaa.db
[09:16:00 INF] SQLite database initialized at data/eetaa.db
[09:16:00 INF] Reset 1003 orphaned in-flight 'processing' settlement(s) to 'pending'
[09:16:00 INF] Current settlement_queue record count: 18924
[09:16:00 INF] Executing Settlement CSV Ingestion phase...
[09:16:00 INF] SingleWriterStorageEngine consumer started.
[09:16:00 INF] Found 17908 eligible settlement(s) for CSV download.
[09:16:06 INF] Progress: 100/17908 settlements (0.6%) | 16.5 item/s | ETA: 00:18:01 | Failed: 0 | Buffer: 1
[09:16:12 INF] Progress: 200/17908 settlements (1.1%) | 16.7 item/s | ETA: 00:17:38 | Failed: 0 | Buffer: 1
[09:16:15 INF] Progress: 251/17908 settlements (1.4%) | 16.7 item/s | ETA: 00:17:35 | Failed: 0 | Buffer: 0
[09:16:20 INF] Progress: 351/17908 settlements (2.0%) | 16.9 item/s | ETA: 00:17:20 | Failed: 0 | Buffer: 0
[09:16:26 INF] Progress: 451/17908 settlements (2.5%) | 16.9 item/s | ETA: 00:17:12 | Failed: 0 | Buffer: 0
[09:16:30 INF] Cancellation requested during settlement save.
[09:16:30 INF] SingleWriterStorageEngine processing canceled.
[09:16:30 INF] SingleWriterStorageEngine consumer stopped. Total processed: 507, errors: 0
[09:16:30 INF] Progress: 507/17908 settlements (2.8%) | 16.9 item/s | ETA: 00:17:10 | Failed: 0 | Buffer: 0
[09:16:45 INF] Progress: 507/17908 settlements (2.8%) | 11.3 item/s | ETA: 00:25:44 | Failed: 0 | Buffer: 261
[09:17:00 INF] Progress: 507/17908 settlements (2.8%) | 8.4 item/s | ETA: 00:34:19 | Failed: 0 | Buffer: 522
[09:17:15 INF] Progress: 507/17908 settlements (2.8%) | 6.8 item/s | ETA: 00:42:54 | Failed: 0 | Buffer: 783
[09:17:30 INF] Progress: 507/17908 settlements (2.8%) | 5.6 item/s | ETA: 00:51:29 | Failed: 0 | Buffer: 1000
[09:17:45 INF] Progress: 507/17908 settlements (2.8%) | 4.8 item/s | ETA: 01:00:03 | Failed: 0 | Buffer: 1000
... (persisted count stays at 507, buffer remains at 1000, ETA expands to 6+ hours)
[09:26:45 INF] Progress: 507/17908 settlements (2.8%) | 0.8 item/s | ETA: 06:08:57 | Failed: 0 | Buffer: 1000
[09:26:51 INF] Channel writer marked complete. Draining pending SQLite write transactions...
[09:26:51 INF] All pending SQLite write transactions committed successfully.
[09:26:51 INF] Worker execution canceled gracefully.
```

## Symptoms & Observed Behavior

1. **Premature Consumer Cancellation / Exit:**
   - At `09:16:30` (30 seconds after starting), `SingleWriterStorageEngine` logs cancellation and exits.
   - Root cause in `Worker.cs`: `using var drainCts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30));` passes a token that cancels after 30 seconds directly to `_storageEngine.ProcessChannelAsync(drainCts.Token)`.
2. **Uncoordinated Producer / Downloader:**
   - `SettlementIngestionService.IngestAsync(stoppingToken)` continues downloading files even though the storage consumer has terminated and is no longer reading from `_channel.Reader`.
   - The buffer increases continuously until hitting capacity (`Buffer: 1000`).
   - The application does not recover, fail fast, or stop downloading once the consumer is dead.

## Expected Behavior

1. The storage engine consumer must not be cancelled after 30 seconds during active ingestion. The 30-second drain timeout should only apply during shutdown/drain after ingestion has completed or cancellation has been requested, not during normal processing.
2. If the storage engine consumer encounters an unrecoverable error or terminates prematurely, the error/cancellation must propagate to stop the ingestion producer immediately.
3. Ingestion should respect channel backpressure and consumer health: when the storage consumer is stopped or the buffer is full, downloading should not run unmonitored.
close_reason: Implemented storage consumer lifecycle and fail-fast coordination in commit 177d205, merged into develop in a80e63b

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief: Storage Consumer Lifecycle & Producer Coordination

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Decouple storage consumer lifetime from drain timeout and coordinate fail-fast producer-consumer lifecycle.

**Current behavior:**
`SingleWriterStorageEngine.ProcessChannelAsync` is initialized with a cancellation token tied to a 30-second timer at startup. After 30 seconds, the consumer cancels and exits while `SettlementIngestionService` continues downloading. Once the 1,000-item channel buffer fills, producers block indefinitely on `EnqueueAsync`, degrading throughput to 0 items/s and deadlocking the worker.

**Desired behavior:**
1. **Unbounded Active Ingestion:** The storage consumer runs for the entire duration of ingestion under the application lifetime token without premature fixed timeouts.
2. **Deferred Drain Timeout:** A bounded drain timeout (30s) applies exclusively during shutdown/drain after the producer finishes and closes the channel writer (`_channel.Complete()`).
3. **Fail-Fast Fault Propagation:** If the storage consumer terminates or faults while ingestion is active, the producer's cancellation token triggers immediately and blocked channel writes unblock to fail fast rather than hanging on backpressure.
4. **Orderly Shutdown & Drain Verification:** On normal completion, all buffered channel items drain and commit to SQLite before shutdown. Incomplete drains log an error.

**Key interfaces:**
- `BackgroundService.ExecuteAsync`: Orchestrates producer and consumer tasks, linking cancellation tokens and enforcing post-completion drain timeouts.
- `ISingleWriterStorageEngine.ProcessChannelAsync(CancellationToken)`: Unmodified stream reader that processes until channel completion or cancellation.
- `ISingleWriterChannel`: Writer completion unblocks awaiting `EnqueueAsync` calls upon consumer termination.
- `ISettlementIngestionService.IngestAsync(CancellationToken)`: Respects linked cancellation and terminates promptly upon consumer failure.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Ingestion processes running longer than 30 seconds continue persisting records without consumer cancellation.
- [ ] The 30-second drain timeout is only armed after HTTP ingestion finishes or host shutdown is initiated.
- [ ] Injecting a consumer failure or early cancellation during ingestion immediately cancels `IngestAsync`, unblocks pending `EnqueueAsync` calls, and causes `Worker` to exit with an error.
- [ ] Normal ingestion runs drain all channel items to SQLite before `Worker.ExecuteAsync` completes.
- [ ] Incomplete drains log an error and leave orphaned `processing` records in a state recoverable by `ResetInFlightProcessingAsync`.
- [ ] Integration tests verify:
  - Ingestion running past 30 seconds without premature consumer cancellation.
  - Immediate producer abort when the storage consumer faults or exits early.
  - Proper drain of buffered channel items upon completion.

**Out of scope:**
- Modifying `ISingleWriterStorageEngine` method signatures.
- Modifying channel capacity limits (1,000 items) or channel backpressure mode.
- SQLite schema, PRAGMA, or transaction boundary changes.
- CSV parsing, network retry policy, or rate-limiting modifications.

comments.author: implementer
comments.text:
### Implementation Report: Storage Consumer Lifecycle & Producer Coordination (#eetaa-7uf)

#### 1. Summary of Changes
Resolved premature storage consumer cancellation and worker deadlock during active ingestion:
- **Decoupled Lifetime from Drain Timeout:** Removed the premature fixed 30s timeout on `drainCts` during initialization in `Worker.cs`. The consumer now runs unbounded during active ingestion under `drainCts.Token`.
- **Linked Producer Cancellation:** Bound `_ingestionService.IngestAsync` to `producerCts`, linked to the host's `stoppingToken`.
- **Deferred Drain Arming:** Armed `_drainTimeout` (30s) exclusively upon host shutdown initiation via `stoppingToken.Register(() => drainCts.CancelAfter(_drainTimeout))` or upon post-producer channel closure in the `finally` block.
- **Fail-Fast Fault Propagation:** Orchestrated `Task.WhenAny(ingestionTask, storageTask)`:
  - If the consumer terminates, faults, or experiences early cancellation while ingestion is active, `producerCts.Cancel()` triggers immediately.
  - `_channel.Complete(consumerEx)` is invoked immediately to unblock pending `EnqueueAsync` calls rather than deadlocking on backpressure.
  - Ingestion unwinds cleanly (suppressing secondary cancellation errors), and the root storage failure propagates to exit with code `1`.
- **Orderly Shutdown & Drain Verification:**
  - Upon normal producer completion, `_channel.Complete()` closes the channel writer.
  - The deferred 30s drain timeout allows pending channel items to commit to SQLite.
  - If items remain or the drain times out, an error is logged (`Channel drain timed out with N item(s) remaining in buffer`).
  - Unpersisted records remain in `status = 'processing'` and are safely recovered by `ResetInFlightProcessingAsync` on subsequent runs.
- **Graceful Host Cancellation:** `catch (OperationCanceledException) when (stoppingToken.IsCancellationRequested)` ensures only clean host shutdown logs graceful exit, while unexpected task cancellations log critical errors and terminate with exit code `1`.

#### 2. Verification & Test Results
- Added comprehensive integration tests in `tests/Eetaa.Worker.Tests/Integration/StorageConsumerLifecycleIntegrationTests.cs`:
  1. `Worker_IngestionRunningPast30Seconds_ContinuesPersistingRecordsWithoutPrematureCancellation`: Confirms active ingestion running >30s (31s delay) processes all records without premature consumer cancellation.
  2. `Worker_ConsumerFaultDuringIngestion_ImmediatelyAbortsProducerAndExitsWithError`: Injects consumer crash; verifies immediate producer abort (<1.5s), channel unblocking, and fatal exit code `1`.
  3. `Worker_ConsumerEarlyExitDuringIngestion_ImmediatelyAbortsProducerAndExitsWithError`: Injects immediate consumer completion; verifies immediate producer abort and exit with code `1`.
  4. `Worker_ConsumerEarlyCancellationDuringIngestion_ImmediatelyAbortsProducerAndExitsWithError`: Injects consumer cancellation; verifies immediate abort and exit with code `1`.
  5. `Worker_DrainsAllBufferedItems_BeforeCompletion`: Verifies all channel items commit to SQLite before shutdown.
  6. `Worker_IncompleteDrain_LogsErrorAndLeavesRecordsInProcessingState`: Verifies drain timeout triggers error log, retains orphaned `processing` records, and recovers them via `ResetInFlightProcessingAsync`.
- Full test suite passed: **71 passed, 0 failed**.

#### 3. Review & Advisor Consultation
- Performed dual code review (`/code-review`) checking Standards (0 ADR violations) and Spec compliance.
- Consulted Technical Advisor: Implementation approved with recommendation to use clean `_channel.Complete()` in `finally` block to guarantee drain logging and preserve root producer exception stack trace. Integrated and verified.

title: Provide visual feedback and progress output during download mode
description:
## Problem Statement

When running the application in `download` mode (`dotnet run --project .\src\Eetaa.Worker\ --mode=download`), there is no visual feedback or ongoing progress output in the console during execution, unlike in `discover` mode.

The user cannot tell whether the application is downloading settlement CSV files, parsing them, or persisting data into the SQLite database.

## Observed Output

```text
└ $ dotnet run --project .\src\Eetaa.Worker\ --mode=download
Using launch settings from .\src\Eetaa.Worker\Properties\launchSettings.json...
Building...
[08:26:27 INF] Worker starting in mode: download, db: data/eetaa.db
[08:26:27 INF] SQLite database initialized at data/eetaa.db
[08:26:27 INF] Current settlement_queue record count: 18924
[08:26:27 INF] Executing Settlement CSV Ingestion phase...
[08:26:27 INF] SingleWriterStorageEngine consumer started.
[08:26:27 INF] Found 18409 eligible settlement(s) for CSV download.
[08:26:57 INF] SingleWriterStorageEngine processing canceled.
[08:26:57 INF] SingleWriterStorageEngine consumer stopped. Total processed: 501, errors: 0
```

Between starting the download phase (`[08:26:27 INF] Found 18409 eligible settlement(s)...`) and stopping (`[08:26:57 INF]...`), no progress, download, parsing, or database write logs are displayed.

## Expected Behavior

The application should provide visual feedback and progress updates during the download/ingestion phase (e.g., periodic progress indicators, items processed, download status, or database persistence metrics), consistent with the feedback given in `discover` mode.
close_reason: Implemented IngestionProgressCoordinator with hybrid cadence progress output, buffer depth tracking, and verified with passing unit/integration tests

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Provide periodic visual feedback and progress metrics during download mode

**Current behavior:**
When running the worker in download mode (`--mode=download` or during the download phase of `--mode=all`), `SettlementIngestionService` loads eligible settlements from `settlement_queue` (often 18,000+ records) and downloads settlement CSV files concurrently while `SingleWriterStorageEngine` writes them to SQLite. From the moment `Found {Count} eligible settlement(s) for CSV download.` is logged until all downloads complete or cancel, zero progress or status log output is emitted at `Information` level, leaving the operator with no visual indication of progress, rate, or health.

**Desired behavior:**
The application must provide periodic, structured console feedback at `Information` level during the ingestion and storage phases. Progress tracking must measure true persistence durability (records committed to SQLite) while observing network progress and channel backlog. Progress should be reported periodically using a hybrid cadence (e.g., every 100 settlements or every 15 seconds, whichever occurs first), as well as upon phase completion or graceful cancellation.

**Key interfaces:**
- `IngestionProgressCoordinator` (or `IngestionProgressTracker`):
  Thread-safe coordinator maintaining total eligible count, downloaded count, persisted count, failed count, start time, and channel backlog. Exposes methods to record download completion and persistence transaction outcomes, and emits formatted progress metrics.
- `SettlementIngestionService`:
  Initializes progress tracking with the batch total and records each downloaded settlement payload.
- `SingleWriterStorageEngine`:
  Notifies the progress coordinator upon committing settlement records (and recording failures) to SQLite.
- Log message format (Serilog `Information` level):
  `Progress: {Persisted}/{Total} settlements ({Percent:F1}%) | {Rate:F1} item/s | ETA: {Eta:hh\:mm\:ss} | Failed: {Failed} | Buffer: {BufferCount}`

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Console displays periodic progress at `Information` level during `--mode=download` showing persisted count, total count, percentage, items/sec throughput, estimated time remaining, error/failure count, and channel buffer depth.
- [ ] Progress reporting triggers at a cadence of every 100 completed items or at least once every 15 seconds while work is active.
- [ ] Final progress summary is logged when ingestion finishes or when cancelled via cancellation token during graceful drain.
- [ ] Small batches (< 100 items) and empty batches (0 items) execute cleanly without hanging timers or emitting redundant/erroneous progress messages.
- [ ] Existing automated unit and integration tests continue to pass.

**Out of scope:**
- Interactive full-screen / ANSI cursor-rewrite progress bars (`Spectre.Console` or raw VT100 control codes).
- Changing SQLite schema or modifying the single-writer channel capacity.
- Modifying discovery mode crawler behavior.

title: Greek Local Authorities (Δήμοι και Κοινότητες) Administrative Changes Ingestion
description:
# Spec: Greek Local Authorities (Δήμοι και Κοινότητες) Administrative Changes Ingestion

## Problem Statement

Users and researchers studying the administrative division history of Greece currently have access to local settlement changes in `eetaa.db`, but lack historical administrative changes for Greek Municipalities and Communities (Δήμοι και Κοινότητες / Local Authorities). EETAA publishes this statutory record online across 937 paginated index pages (`dk_metaboles.php`) and individual authority CSV export endpoints (`dkmet2csv.php?sid={id}`). Manually querying and compiling these records across thousands of authorities is impractical, and the current worker application only targets settlements. Users need the existing application enhanced to autonomously harvest, normalize, and store local authority administrative changes in a dedicated table alongside existing settlement data.

## Solution

Enhance the `Eetaa.Worker` application to harvest Greek Local Authority administrative changes into a dedicated `dkmet_details` SQLite table and manage crawl state in a `local_authority_queue` table. The solution introduces an `--entity` CLI option (`all`, `settlements`, `authorities`, defaulting to `all`) that seamlessly integrates with existing `--mode` phases (`all`, `discover`, `download`). For local authorities, index discovery harvests authority identifiers directly from pagination pages (`dk_metaboles.php`), and ingestion streams CSV records directly from `dkmet2csv.php?sid={id}` via a dedicated Single-Writer Channel into SQLite, guaranteeing zero lock contention and transactional durability.

## User Stories

1. As a data analyst, I want the worker to crawl the EETAA local authority index pagination, so that all valid municipality and community identifiers and name hints are discovered without scanning non-existent IDs.
2. As a data analyst, I want discovered local authorities stored in a `local_authority_queue` table with lifecycle status, so that I can inspect discovery progress and know how many local authorities exist.
3. As a database user, I want duplicate local authority entries across index pages (due to multiple historical names or regional reassignments) deduplicated by authority ID, so that the queue maintains exactly one record per unique authority.
4. As a data analyst, I want the worker to download the administrative change CSV for each queued local authority directly from the CSV endpoint, so that all historical transitions are captured locally without unnecessary requests to intermediate detail pages.
5. As an operator running a long crawl, I want the worker to resume where it left off if interrupted, so that already completed local authorities are not re-downloaded.
6. As a system operator, I want transient network failures and HTTP 502/504/429 responses during authority crawling and CSV downloading to be automatically retried with exponential backoff and jitter, so that temporary remote hiccups do not crash the crawl.
7. As an operator, I want local authorities that fail repeatedly to be marked as `failed` with the error reason recorded, so that unrecoverable issues can be inspected and retried later.
8. As a consumer of Greek administrative data, I want each administrative change for a local authority stored as a distinct row in `dkmet_details` maintaining chronological order, so that I can track transitions over time.
9. As a data researcher, I want the statutory entity type (Municipality or Community) preserved as `ota_type` in `dkmet_details`, so that I can distinguish whether an administrative event pertains to a municipality (`Δ`) or a community (`Κ`).
10. As an SQL query author, I want FEK publication dates normalized from `DD/MM/YYYY` to ISO-8601 (`YYYY-MM-DD`) format, so that I can run chronological date filtering and `BETWEEN` queries on local authority changes in SQLite.
11. As a data analyst, I want FEK dates that deviate from standard date formats (such as partial historical records like `//1924` or `-`) preserved safely as sanitized strings rather than failing the import, so that no historical records are lost.
12. As a database administrator, I want foreign keys enabled in SQLite alongside WAL mode and NORMAL synchronous settings, so that relational integrity between `local_authority_queue` and `dkmet_details` is enforced.
13. As a system administrator, I want concurrent HTTP downloads for local authorities decoupled from SQLite writes via a dedicated single-writer channel, so that the application never encounters `SQLITE_BUSY` database lock errors under load.
14. As an operator, I want the worker to cleanly handle empty (header-only) CSV exports for local authorities with no recorded changes, marking them as completed without throwing errors.
15. As an operator, I want an `--entity` CLI flag (`--entity=all|settlements|authorities`, default `all`), so that I can target either settlements, local authorities, or both in a single run.
16. As an operator, I want the `--entity` flag composable with `--mode` (`--mode=all|discover|download`), so that I can selectively run index discovery or CSV downloading for local authorities independently.
17. As an operator running with `--entity=all`, I want the pipeline to execute sequentially per entity (Settlements fully processed, then Local Authorities fully processed), so that intermediate progress is durable and failure in one domain does not corrupt the other.
18. As an operator, I want flags like `--retry-failed` and `--force` to apply cleanly to local authorities when targeted, so that I can reprocess failed or existing authorities on demand.
19. As an operator, I want orphaned `processing` records in `local_authority_queue` automatically reset to `pending` on worker startup, so that crashes or forced shutdowns do not leave tasks permanently blocked.
20. As an operator running the worker interactively, I want graceful shutdown on Ctrl+C during authority processing, so that in-flight database transactions commit safely before the application terminates.
21. As a developer debugging issues, I want structured Serilog console logging with entity-specific progress metrics and timestamps, so that I can monitor crawl throughput for both settlements and local authorities.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Domain Model Alignment**: Uses canonical terms established in `CONTEXT.md`: Local Authority, Authority Type, Local Authority Queue, Administrative Change, Government Gazette (FEK), and Prefecture (Nomos). In C# domain code, statutory status is modeled as `AuthorityType` while persisting to database column `ota_type` and mapping to CSV header `"ΕΙΔΟΣ ΟΤΑ"`.
- **Database Schema**:
  - `local_authority_queue` table:
    - `authority_id` (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY)
    - `name_hint` (TEXT)
    - `status` (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'processing', 'completed', 'failed')))
    - `attempt_count` (INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0)
    - `last_attempt_at` (TEXT NULL)
    - `completed_at` (TEXT NULL)
    - `error_message` (TEXT NULL)
    - `created_at` (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now')))
    - `updated_at` (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now')))
    - Index on `status`.
  - `dkmet_details` table:
    - `authority_id` (INTEGER NOT NULL)
    - `change_order` (INTEGER NOT NULL)
    - `ota_type` (TEXT NULL)
    - `authority_name` (TEXT NOT NULL)
    - `nomos` (TEXT NULL)
    - `change_year` (INTEGER NULL)
    - `fek_number` (TEXT NULL)
    - `fek_issue` (TEXT NULL)
    - `fek_date` (TEXT NULL) - normalized ISO-8601 `YYYY-MM-DD`
    - `fek_date_raw` (TEXT NULL)
    - `change_description` (TEXT NOT NULL)
    - `raw_record` (TEXT NULL)
    - `created_at` (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now')))
    - PRIMARY KEY (`authority_id`, `change_order`)
    - FOREIGN KEY (`authority_id`) REFERENCES `local_authority_queue`(`authority_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE
    - Indices on `authority_id` and `fek_date`.
- **Database Access & Concurrency Guardrails**:
  - Direct ADO.NET using `Microsoft.Data.Sqlite`.
  - SQLite initialized with `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;`, `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL;`, and `PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL;`.
  - Startup in-flight recovery executes:
    `UPDATE settlement_queue SET status = 'pending' WHERE status = 'processing';`
    `UPDATE local_authority_queue SET status = 'pending' WHERE status = 'processing';`
- **CSV Ingestion & Direct Endpoint Targeting**:
  - Direct targeting of `https://eetaa.gr/eetaa/metaboles/dkmet2csv.php?sid={id}` based on IDs discovered from index pages, skipping `dkmet_details.php` HTML retrieval.
  - Dedicated `LocalAuthorityCsvParser` (or generalized schema-driven parser) supporting 8 columns: `"ΕΙΔΟΣ ΟΤΑ"`, `"ΟΝΟΜΑΣΙΑ ΟΤΑ"`, `ΝΟΜΟΣ`, `"ΕΤΟΣ ΜΕΤΑΒΟΛΗΣ"`, `"ΑΡΙΘΜΟΣ ΦΕΚ"`, `"ΤΕΥΧΟΣ ΦΕΚ"`, `"ΗΜΕΡΟΜΗΝΙΑ ΦΕΚ"`, `"ΠΕΡΙΓΡΑΦΗ ΜΕΤΑΒΟΛΗΣ"`.
  - Robust multi-pass date parsing using existing `FekDateParser`.
- **Multi-Entity CLI & Pipeline Orchestration**:
  - CLI flag `--entity` (`all` [default], `settlements`, `authorities`) composable with `--mode` (`all`, `discover`, `download`).
  - Configuration separates default endpoint URLs (`SettlementsBaseUrl`, `AuthoritiesBaseUrl`) rather than overloading a single string.
  - Ingestion writes use the Single-Writer Channel pattern with scoped channel and consumer lifecycles per active ingestion stage (rather than singleton instances in DI), preventing re-entrancy channel closure (`ChannelClosedException`) across sequential entity runs and guaranteeing clean channel completion and timeout draining.
  - Ingestion progress coordinator (`IngestionProgressCoordinator`) is parameterized with the target entity label ("settlement" or "local authority") to ensure accurate logging and console metrics per User Story 21.

## Testing Decisions

- **Testing Philosophy & Seams**:
  - Tests verify observable external behavior and persisted state in SQLite without asserting on private implementation details.
  - Primary Seam (Top-level Integration):
    - `EndToEndWorkerLifecycleTests`: Uses real SQLite in a temporary file and a mock HTTP handler to execute the worker across all permutations of `--entity` (`settlements`, `authorities`, `all`) and `--mode` (`discover`, `download`, `all`). Verifies queue population and details table rows.
  - Subordinate Unit Seams:
    - `LocalAuthorityCsvParserTests`: Verifies parsing of standard 8-column authority CSVs, empty/header-only files, UTF-8 BOM handling, and irregular date strings.
    - `IndexParserTests`: Verifies parsing of `dk_metaboles.php` HTML tables, extraction of `dkmet_details.php?id={id}`, deduplication across multiple occurrences of the same authority ID, and pagination parsing up to page 937.
    - `WorkerCliOptionsTests`: Verifies correct parsing of `--entity` and defaults.

## Out of Scope

- Scraping prefecture-level (`nom_metaboles.php`) administrative changes.
- Downloading PDF copies of Government Gazette issues (`dkmet2pdf.php` or `fek_*.pdf`).
- Web-based user interface or dashboard.
- Live internet network access during automated CI test execution (all tests must use local fixtures and mock HTTP handlers).

## Further Notes

- Documented in `CONTEXT.md` (domain language) and `docs/adr/0005-local-authority-ingestion-and-multi-entity-pipeline.md`.

title: Local Authority Discovery & Queue Persistence
description:
## Parent

title: EETAA Settlement Administrative History Worker
description:
## Problem Statement

Users and researchers studying administrative divisions in Greece lack a unified, queryable, local relational dataset of historical administrative changes for Greek settlements (such as renamings, annexations, municipal mergers, and transfers across prefectures). EETAA publishes this historical record online across 2,247 paginated directory pages and individual settlement CSV download endpoints. However, manually querying, downloading, and correlating these tens of thousands of records is impractical, fragile, and prone to network and rate-limiting failures.

## Solution

A robust, resilient .NET 10 console worker application (`Eetaa.Worker`) that autonomously harvests settlement identifiers from the EETAA inventory and downloads their administrative change histories into a local SQLite database (`data/eetaa.db`). The worker operates with two distinct, resumable phases (Index Discovery and Settlement CSV Ingestion), decouples concurrent network downloads from single-writer SQLite transactions via an in-memory channel to prevent lock contention, and provides a fully normalized, queryable `oikmet_details` table.

## User Stories

1. As a data analyst, I want the worker to crawl the EETAA settlement index pagination, so that all valid settlement identifiers and name hints are discovered without guessing or scanning non-existent IDs.
2. As a data analyst, I want discovered settlements stored in a `settlement_queue` table with lifecycle status, so that I can inspect discovery progress and know how many settlements exist.
3. As a database user, I want duplicate settlement entries across index pages (due to multiple historical aliases) deduplicated by settlement ID, so that the queue maintains exactly one record per unique settlement.
4. As a data analyst, I want the worker to download the administrative change CSV for each queued settlement, so that all historical transitions are captured locally.
5. As an operator running a long crawl, I want the worker to resume where it left off if interrupted, so that already completed settlements are not re-downloaded.
6. As a system operator, I want transient network failures and HTTP 502/504/429 responses to be automatically retried with exponential backoff and jitter, so that temporary remote hiccups do not crash the crawl.
7. As an operator, I want settlements that fail repeatedly to be marked as `failed` with the error reason recorded, so that unrecoverable issues can be inspected and retried later.
8. As a consumer of Greek administrative data, I want each administrative change stored as a distinct row in `oikmet_details` maintaining chronological order, so that I can track transitions over time.
9. As an SQL query author, I want FEK publication dates normalized from `DD/MM/YYYY` to ISO-8601 (`YYYY-MM-DD`) format, so that I can run chronological date filtering and `BETWEEN` queries in SQLite.
10. As a data analyst, I want FEK dates that deviate from standard date formats (such as partial historical records) preserved safely as sanitized strings rather than failing the settlement import, so that no historical records are lost.
11. As a database administrator, I want SQLite to run in WAL mode with normalized synchronous settings, so that read queries can execute concurrently without blocking ingestion.
12. As a system administrator, I want concurrent HTTP downloads decoupled from SQLite writes via a single-writer channel, so that the application never encounters `SQLITE_BUSY` database lock errors under load.
13. As an operator, I want the worker to cleanly handle empty (header-only) CSV exports for settlements with no recorded changes, marking them as completed without throwing errors.
14. As an operator, I want CLI flags (`--mode=all`, `--mode=discover`, `--mode=download`), so that I can selectively run index discovery or CSV downloading independently.
15. As an operator, I want flags like `--retry-failed` and `--force`, so that I can reprocess failed or existing settlements on demand.
16. As an operator, I want orphaned `processing` records automatically reset to `pending` on worker startup, so that crashes or forced shutdowns do not leave tasks permanently blocked.
17. As an operator running the worker interactively, I want graceful shutdown on Ctrl+C, so that in-flight database transactions commit safely before the application terminates.
18. As a developer debugging issues, I want structured Serilog console logging with timestamps and progress metrics, so that I can monitor crawl throughput and inspect warnings.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Domain Model Alignment**: Uses canonical terms established in the domain glossary: Settlement, Administrative Change, Government Gazette (FEK), Prefecture (Nomos), and Settlement Queue.
- **Two-Phase Architecture**:
  - Phase 1 (Index Discovery): Discovers settlement entries by requesting `oik_metaboles.php?ltr=ALL&pg={page}` across pages 1..2247, extracting links matching `oikmet_details.php?id={id}`, and performing bulk upsert into `settlement_queue`.
  - Phase 2 (CSV Ingestion): Pulls eligible items from `settlement_queue`, downloads CSVs from `oikmet2csv.php?sid={id}`, parses them, and commits normalized records into `oikmet_details`.
- **Database Schema**:
  - `settlement_queue` schema:
    - `settlement_id` (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY)
    - `name_hint` (TEXT)
    - `status` (TEXT NOT NULL, checked for 'pending', 'processing', 'completed', 'failed')
    - `attempt_count` (INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0)
    - `last_attempt_at` (TEXT)
    - `completed_at` (TEXT)
    - `last_error` (TEXT)
    - Index on `status`.
  - `oikmet_details` schema:
    - `settlement_id` (INTEGER NOT NULL)
    - `change_order` (INTEGER NOT NULL)
    - `settlement_name` (TEXT NOT NULL)
    - `nomos` (TEXT)
    - `change_year` (INTEGER)
    - `fek_number` (TEXT)
    - `fek_issue` (TEXT)
    - `fek_date` (TEXT) - ISO-8601 `YYYY-MM-DD` when parseable, raw fallback otherwise
    - `change_description` (TEXT NOT NULL)
    - `created_at` (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
    - PRIMARY KEY (`settlement_id`, `change_order`)
    - FOREIGN KEY (`settlement_id`) REFERENCES `settlement_queue`(`settlement_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE
- **Data Access & Storage Engine**: Pure ADO.NET using `Microsoft.Data.Sqlite` without ORM or micro-ORM overhead. SQLite initialized with `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;`, `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON;`, and `PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL;`.
- **Concurrency & SQLite Single-Writer Pattern**:
  - HTTP requests run concurrently with throttled concurrency (default 3 concurrent workers) and polite delay (100–250ms).
  - Downloaded CSV payloads are parsed and published to a bounded `System.Threading.Channels.Channel<SettlementBatch>`.
  - A single dedicated database consumer task reads from the channel and executes per-settlement atomic transactions (`DELETE FROM oikmet_details WHERE settlement_id = @id; INSERT INTO oikmet_details ...; UPDATE settlement_queue ...;`), completely eliminating `SQLITE_BUSY` contention.
- **CSV Parsing Engine**: Uses `CsvHelper` with UTF-8 BOM awareness, semicolon (`;`) delimiter, Greek culture support, and field sanitization. Blank FEK numbers or issues are normalized to `NULL`.
- **Crash Recovery**: On startup, any queue items left in `processing` status are reverted: `UPDATE settlement_queue SET status = 'pending' WHERE status = 'processing';`.
- **CLI & Configuration Options**:
  - Configurable via `appsettings.json` and CLI arguments: `--mode` (`all`, `discover`, `download`), `--db` (default `data/eetaa.db`), `--concurrency` (default 3), `--delay-ms` (default 150), `--retry-failed` (boolean), `--force` (boolean).
- **Project Structure**: Standard .NET 10 Worker Service in `src/Eetaa.Worker/` managed by root solution `eetaa.sln` and governed by root `.editorconfig`.

## Testing Decisions

- **Testing Philosophy & Seams**:
  - Tests will focus strictly on observable external behavior at the highest meaningful seams, avoiding assertions on private implementation details.
  - Primary Seams:
    1. **HTTP Ingestion & Pipeline Seam**: A mock HTTP message handler responding with recorded EETAA index HTML pages and CSV payloads, verifying the end-to-end outcome in SQLite (records in `settlement_queue` and `oikmet_details`).
    2. **CSV & Date Normalizer Seam**: Testing CSV parsing against real-world sample responses (standard changes, header-only empty files, irregular FEK dates, multi-line quoted Greek descriptions).
    3. **Resilience & Resumption Seam**: Testing interrupted crawl recovery (interrupted `processing` reset to `pending`, idempotency on duplicate imports, and failure state transitions).
- **Target Modules to Test**:
  - Pipeline orchestrator / worker service against SQLite test database (`data/test_eetaa.db` or temporary file).
  - Settlement CSV parser & date converter.
  - SQLite queue and details repository.

## Out of Scope

- Scraping municipality (`dkmet_details.php`) or prefecture level metaboles.
- PDF downloads of Government Gazette issues (`oikmet2pdf.php` or `fek_*.pdf`).
- Graphical user interface or web dashboard for viewing changes.
- Automated scheduling via external CRON or Windows Task Scheduler (handled externally by the host system).

## Further Notes

- Historical administrative changes in Greece frequently cross boundary changes from Kapodistrias (1997) and Kallikratis (2010) municipal reforms.
- All technical architecture decisions are recorded in ADRs 0001 through 0004 under `docs/adr/`.

title: Add root README.md describing application function and CLI options
description:
## Context & Problem
Currently, there is no `README.md` file in the root of the repository. A human user encountering the project lacks immediate documentation describing what the application does, how it functions, and how to run or use it.

## Scope of Work
1. Add a comprehensive `README.md` file in the repository root.
2. Clearly describe the application's function and purpose (crawling, discovery, and ingestion of Greek settlement administrative changes published by EETAA into a local SQLite database).
3. Document prerequisite requirements (such as .NET SDK version) and instructions for building and running the application.
4. Document all supported command-line options parsed by `WorkerCliOptions`:
   - `--mode` / `--mode=<mode>`: Execution mode (`all`, `discover`, `download`; default: `all`).
   - `--db` / `--db=<path>`: SQLite database file path (default: `data/eetaa.db`).
   - `--base-url` / `--base-url=<url>`: Target EETAA endpoint URL (default: `https://eetaa.gr/eetaa/metaboles/oik_metaboles.php`).
   - `--concurrency` / `--concurrency=<n>`: Concurrency level for worker operations (default: `3`).
   - `--delay-ms` / `--delay-ms=<ms>`: Polite request delay in milliseconds (default: `150`).
   - `--start-page` / `--start-page=<n>`: Start page number for index discovery (default: `1`).
   - `--max-pages` / `--max-pages=<n>`: Maximum number of index pages to crawl.
   - `--retry-failed`: Flag to re-queue failed settlement tasks for another attempt.
   - `--force`: Flag to force re-download/re-ingestion of already processed settlements.
5. Provide practical usage examples demonstrating common operational workflows (e.g. running full pipeline, running discovery only, running download only, specifying custom database path).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `README.md` exists in the repo root with clear markdown structure and human-friendly documentation.
- Application function and architecture overview are accurately described.
- All CLI options from `WorkerCliOptions.cs` are documented with their purpose, expected types, and default values.
- Example commands are provided and verified.

title: EETAA Settlement Administrative History Worker
description:
## Problem Statement

Users and researchers studying administrative divisions in Greece lack a unified, queryable, local relational dataset of historical administrative changes for Greek settlements (such as renamings, annexations, municipal mergers, and transfers across prefectures). EETAA publishes this historical record online across 2,247 paginated directory pages and individual settlement CSV download endpoints. However, manually querying, downloading, and correlating these tens of thousands of records is impractical, fragile, and prone to network and rate-limiting failures.

## Solution

A robust, resilient .NET 10 console worker application (`Eetaa.Worker`) that autonomously harvests settlement identifiers from the EETAA inventory and downloads their administrative change histories into a local SQLite database (`data/eetaa.db`). The worker operates with two distinct, resumable phases (Index Discovery and Settlement CSV Ingestion), decouples concurrent network downloads from single-writer SQLite transactions via an in-memory channel to prevent lock contention, and provides a fully normalized, queryable `oikmet_details` table.

## User Stories

1. As a data analyst, I want the worker to crawl the EETAA settlement index pagination, so that all valid settlement identifiers and name hints are discovered without guessing or scanning non-existent IDs.
2. As a data analyst, I want discovered settlements stored in a `settlement_queue` table with lifecycle status, so that I can inspect discovery progress and know how many settlements exist.
3. As a database user, I want duplicate settlement entries across index pages (due to multiple historical aliases) deduplicated by settlement ID, so that the queue maintains exactly one record per unique settlement.
4. As a data analyst, I want the worker to download the administrative change CSV for each queued settlement, so that all historical transitions are captured locally.
5. As an operator running a long crawl, I want the worker to resume where it left off if interrupted, so that already completed settlements are not re-downloaded.
6. As a system operator, I want transient network failures and HTTP 502/504/429 responses to be automatically retried with exponential backoff and jitter, so that temporary remote hiccups do not crash the crawl.
7. As an operator, I want settlements that fail repeatedly to be marked as `failed` with the error reason recorded, so that unrecoverable issues can be inspected and retried later.
8. As a consumer of Greek administrative data, I want each administrative change stored as a distinct row in `oikmet_details` maintaining chronological order, so that I can track transitions over time.
9. As an SQL query author, I want FEK publication dates normalized from `DD/MM/YYYY` to ISO-8601 (`YYYY-MM-DD`) format, so that I can run chronological date filtering and `BETWEEN` queries in SQLite.
10. As a data analyst, I want FEK dates that deviate from standard date formats (such as partial historical records) preserved safely as sanitized strings rather than failing the settlement import, so that no historical records are lost.
11. As a database administrator, I want SQLite to run in WAL mode with normalized synchronous settings, so that read queries can execute concurrently without blocking ingestion.
12. As a system administrator, I want concurrent HTTP downloads decoupled from SQLite writes via a single-writer channel, so that the application never encounters `SQLITE_BUSY` database lock errors under load.
13. As an operator, I want the worker to cleanly handle empty (header-only) CSV exports for settlements with no recorded changes, marking them as completed without throwing errors.
14. As an operator, I want CLI flags (`--mode=all`, `--mode=discover`, `--mode=download`), so that I can selectively run index discovery or CSV downloading independently.
15. As an operator, I want flags like `--retry-failed` and `--force`, so that I can reprocess failed or existing settlements on demand.
16. As an operator, I want orphaned `processing` records automatically reset to `pending` on worker startup, so that crashes or forced shutdowns do not leave tasks permanently blocked.
17. As an operator running the worker interactively, I want graceful shutdown on Ctrl+C, so that in-flight database transactions commit safely before the application terminates.
18. As a developer debugging issues, I want structured Serilog console logging with timestamps and progress metrics, so that I can monitor crawl throughput and inspect warnings.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Domain Model Alignment**: Uses canonical terms established in the domain glossary: Settlement, Administrative Change, Government Gazette (FEK), Prefecture (Nomos), and Settlement Queue.
- **Two-Phase Architecture**:
  - Phase 1 (Index Discovery): Discovers settlement entries by requesting `oik_metaboles.php?ltr=ALL&pg={page}` across pages 1..2247, extracting links matching `oikmet_details.php?id={id}`, and performing bulk upsert into `settlement_queue`.
  - Phase 2 (CSV Ingestion): Pulls eligible items from `settlement_queue`, downloads CSVs from `oikmet2csv.php?sid={id}`, parses them, and commits normalized records into `oikmet_details`.
- **Database Schema**:
  - `settlement_queue` schema:
    - `settlement_id` (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY)
    - `name_hint` (TEXT)
    - `status` (TEXT NOT NULL, checked for 'pending', 'processing', 'completed', 'failed')
    - `attempt_count` (INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0)
    - `last_attempt_at` (TEXT)
    - `completed_at` (TEXT)
    - `last_error` (TEXT)
    - Index on `status`.
  - `oikmet_details` schema:
    - `settlement_id` (INTEGER NOT NULL)
    - `change_order` (INTEGER NOT NULL)
    - `settlement_name` (TEXT NOT NULL)
    - `nomos` (TEXT)
    - `change_year` (INTEGER)
    - `fek_number` (TEXT)
    - `fek_issue` (TEXT)
    - `fek_date` (TEXT) - ISO-8601 `YYYY-MM-DD` when parseable, raw fallback otherwise
    - `change_description` (TEXT NOT NULL)
    - `created_at` (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
    - PRIMARY KEY (`settlement_id`, `change_order`)
    - FOREIGN KEY (`settlement_id`) REFERENCES `settlement_queue`(`settlement_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE
- **Data Access & Storage Engine**: Pure ADO.NET using `Microsoft.Data.Sqlite` without ORM or micro-ORM overhead. SQLite initialized with `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;`, `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON;`, and `PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL;`.
- **Concurrency & SQLite Single-Writer Pattern**:
  - HTTP requests run concurrently with throttled concurrency (default 3 concurrent workers) and polite delay (100–250ms).
  - Downloaded CSV payloads are parsed and published to a bounded `System.Threading.Channels.Channel<SettlementBatch>`.
  - A single dedicated database consumer task reads from the channel and executes per-settlement atomic transactions (`DELETE FROM oikmet_details WHERE settlement_id = @id; INSERT INTO oikmet_details ...; UPDATE settlement_queue ...;`), completely eliminating `SQLITE_BUSY` contention.
- **CSV Parsing Engine**: Uses `CsvHelper` with UTF-8 BOM awareness, semicolon (`;`) delimiter, Greek culture support, and field sanitization. Blank FEK numbers or issues are normalized to `NULL`.
- **Crash Recovery**: On startup, any queue items left in `processing` status are reverted: `UPDATE settlement_queue SET status = 'pending' WHERE status = 'processing';`.
- **CLI & Configuration Options**:
  - Configurable via `appsettings.json` and CLI arguments: `--mode` (`all`, `discover`, `download`), `--db` (default `data/eetaa.db`), `--concurrency` (default 3), `--delay-ms` (default 150), `--retry-failed` (boolean), `--force` (boolean).
- **Project Structure**: Standard .NET 10 Worker Service in `src/Eetaa.Worker/` managed by root solution `eetaa.sln` and governed by root `.editorconfig`.

## Testing Decisions

- **Testing Philosophy & Seams**:
  - Tests will focus strictly on observable external behavior at the highest meaningful seams, avoiding assertions on private implementation details.
  - Primary Seams:
    1. **HTTP Ingestion & Pipeline Seam**: A mock HTTP message handler responding with recorded EETAA index HTML pages and CSV payloads, verifying the end-to-end outcome in SQLite (records in `settlement_queue` and `oikmet_details`).
    2. **CSV & Date Normalizer Seam**: Testing CSV parsing against real-world sample responses (standard changes, header-only empty files, irregular FEK dates, multi-line quoted Greek descriptions).
    3. **Resilience & Resumption Seam**: Testing interrupted crawl recovery (interrupted `processing` reset to `pending`, idempotency on duplicate imports, and failure state transitions).
- **Target Modules to Test**:
  - Pipeline orchestrator / worker service against SQLite test database (`data/test_eetaa.db` or temporary file).
  - Settlement CSV parser & date converter.
  - SQLite queue and details repository.

## Out of Scope

- Scraping municipality (`dkmet_details.php`) or prefecture level metaboles.
- PDF downloads of Government Gazette issues (`oikmet2pdf.php` or `fek_*.pdf`).
- Graphical user interface or web dashboard for viewing changes.
- Automated scheduling via external CRON or Windows Task Scheduler (handled externally by the host system).

## Further Notes

- Historical administrative changes in Greece frequently cross boundary changes from Kapodistrias (1997) and Kallikratis (2010) municipal reforms.
- All technical architecture decisions are recorded in ADRs 0001 through 0004 under `docs/adr/`.
